S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

info.persona: Antonio Fung, a 65‑year‑old blues‑loving gardener‑painter, they fuse eclectic culinary experiments with spontaneous art, volunteer storytelling, and a habit of juggling a loosely kept notebook of worries while still finding joy in weekly music nights and backyard harvests.
info.professional_persona: Antonio Fung, a retired handyman‑mentor who volunteers as a community storyteller, they blend practical DIY expertise with a curious, improvisational spirit to guide teenagers through oral‑history projects while also helping expand the neighborhood garden initiative.
info.cultural_background: Antonio was born and raised in Memphis to a multicultural family—his father was African‑American, his mother was of Cuban‑Latino descent, and his maternal grandmother was a Chinese immigrant who settled in the South after World War II. Growing up, he absorbed the rhythms of the city’s blues scene, the vibrant flavors of Southern soul food, the spice‑laden dishes of his Latin heritage, and the subtle techniques of Chinese cooking taught by his grandmother. His family celebrates a blend of traditions: church services on Sundays, annual Juneteenth gatherings, Cuban music festivals, and Chinese New Year meals. This rich tapestry of influences informs his worldview, his culinary experiments, and his reverence for artistic expression across cultures.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Antonio spends his free time immersed in music, especially blues, jazz, and soul, often attending live performances at Beale Street venues or listening to vinyl records at home. He enjoys painting landscapes and abstract pieces, letting his imagination guide him without strict plans. Gardening provides both relaxation and a sense of purpose; his backyard hosts tomatoes, collard greens, and herbs that he uses in his cooking experiments. Cooking is a creative outlet—he frequently blends Southern, Mexican, and Chinese flavors into new dishes, sharing them with friends and family. He also likes strolling through local art galleries, reading biographies of artists and activists, and capturing candid moments with his DSLR camera. Occasionally, he writes short reflections in a journal to process worries and track personal growth.
info.sports_persona: Antonio Fung, an avid walker and casual tennis enthusiast, they enjoy early morning strolls through his garden, join a senior‑friendly tai‑chi class on Tuesdays, and rally behind the Memphis Grizzlies while occasionally catching a Memphis Redbirds baseball game.
info.arts_persona: Antonio Fung, a soulful blues aficionado and amateur painter, they study the improvisations of Miles Davis, admire the brushwork of Claude Monet and Georgia O'Keeffe, peruse local galleries featuring works by contemporary Southern artists, and channel these influences into vibrant abstract landscapes.
info.travel_persona: Antonio Fung, an inquisitive senior traveler, they plan relaxed, culturally immersive trips such as a week‑long visit to Washington, D.C. to explore the Smithsonian American Art Museum and a major history museum on the National Mall, a music‑laden weekend in New Orleans’ French Quarter, and a scenic road‑trip to the desert galleries of Santa Fe, balancing modest savings with occasional grant‑funded group travel.
info.culinary_persona: Antonio Fung, a creative home chef, they blend Southern, Mexican, and Asian flavors to craft dishes like collard‑green stir‑fry with chipotle glaze, tomato‑basil tamales, and ginger‑infused fried chicken, regularly experiment with fresh tomatoes, herbs, and spices from his garden, and delight friends and family with pop‑up tastings that showcase his culinary curiosity.

info.persona: Sherryann Johnson blends scientific curiosity, dance‑floor energy, and a laid‑back, sometimes chaotic, approach to life, turning spontaneous adventures into community‑focused projects while juggling occasional forgetfulness.
info.professional_persona: Sherryann Johnson, a budding data analyst at a San Antonio biotech startup, leverages her Python, R, and molecular biology background to turn complex health data into actionable community insights, while her sociable, collaborative nature shines in agile team settings, even if her relaxed attitude toward deadlines sometimes leads to all‑night coding marathons.
info.cultural_background: Sherryann was raised in a predominantly white, middle‑class family in San Antonio, blending mainstream American values with the distinctive hospitality and community spirit of Texas. Growing up amidst a multicultural city, she has absorbed elements of local Mexican culture—especially in food, music, and communal celebrations—while maintaining her family's traditions of independence, volunteerism, and academic achievement. This hybrid background informs her inclusive outlook, her love for group activities, and her desire to contribute positively to the diverse community around her.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Sherryann thrives on social and active pursuits. She frequently joins friends for salsa dancing nights and enjoys exploring the Texas Hill Country on hikes. She volunteers at local STEM outreach events, helping middle‑school students discover science and technology. Music festivals, cooking Tex‑Mex dishes, and attending hackathons or coding meetups also keep her energized. When she wants quiet time, she reads popular‑science books or browses art galleries around San Antonio.
info.sports_persona: Sherryann Johnson, an enthusiastic member of the San Antonio Salsa Social Club and a weekend hiker exploring the Texas Hill Country, passionately supports the San Antonio Spurs and follows the Texas Rangers, though her disorganized schedule sometimes causes missed gym workouts.
info.arts_persona: Sherryann Johnson, a regular at San Antonio’s vibrant mural tours and a fan of Bad Bunny, Beyoncé, and the indie folk duo Lord Huron, infuses her love for music into spontaneous salsa dance performances at local art galleries.
info.travel_persona: Sherryann Johnson, an adventurous road‑tripper who has visited Austin, New Mexico, and Barcelona, dreams of hiking Patagonia’s Torres del Paine and often books flights at the last minute, sacrificing early‑bird savings for the thrill of spontaneous travel.
info.culinary_persona: Sherryann Johnson, a self‑taught Tex‑Mex chef who perfects fish tacos with fresh cilantro, lime, and chipotle aioli, often experiments with homemade salsas but occasionally forgets to restock tortillas after impromptu dinner parties.

info.persona: Daniel Dorta blends disciplined sales leadership with an abstract artist’s imagination, juggling spreadsheet precision and midnight guitar riffs while habitually sketching SOPs on napkins.
info.professional_persona: Daniel Dorta, a 36‑year‑old sales leader, directs non‑retail teams using a blend of disciplined Lean Six Sigma methodology and vivid abstract thinking; their bilingual fluency lets them craft data‑driven training programs that boost performance while keeping morale high, and they are actively mapping a path toward regional management and a future consulting venture.
info.cultural_background: Daniel’s Spanish heritage is a core part of his identity; he grew up in a bilingual household where Spanish language, Catholic traditions, and family gatherings were central. Living in Gallup, New Mexico, he has also absorbed the rich tapestry of Southwestern and Native American cultures, appreciating local art, music, and community celebrations. He blends these influences in his daily life, from the foods he prepares to the festivals he attends, and his bilingual fluency helps him navigate both Hispanic and broader American contexts at work and in his community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In his free time, Daniel channels his imagination into abstract painting and guitar playing, often exploring Spanish folk melodies. He enjoys reading philosophy, contemporary science‑fiction, and design theory, which fuel his creative approach at work. Outdoor pursuits such as desert hiking and landscape photography allow him to capture the vast New Mexican scenery. He is also an avid cook, experimenting with traditional Spanish tapas and Southwestern dishes, and he participates in local art festivals and cultural events.
info.sports_persona: Daniel Dorta fuels fitness through regular desert treks with the New Mexico Outdoor Club, occasional trail runs, and follows New Mexico United soccer and the Albuquerque Isotopes baseball teams, balancing a disciplined training schedule with the relaxed mindset of a landscape photographer.
info.arts_persona: Daniel Dorta channels imagination onto canvas with abstract compositions inspired by Mark Rothko while strumming Spanish folk melodies à la Paco de Lucía on guitar, regularly attending the Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta’s art installations and infusing contemporary sci‑fi narratives into creative pursuits.
info.travel_persona: Daniel Dorta plans trips with a spreadsheet of must‑see vistas, from spontaneous weekend escapes to Sedona’s red rocks to meticulously organized journeys through Granada’s historic Albayzín, balancing a modest travel budget with a yearning for both desert solitude and European cultural immersion.
info.culinary_persona: Daniel Dorta, an adept home chef, fuses traditional Spanish tapas such as patatas bravas and jamón ibérico with Southwestern favorites like chile relleno and green chile stew, often seasoning dishes with smoked paprika and fresh pomegranate seeds to craft bold, layered flavors.
